contract_implemented.freeze: ReviewedProposalService::freeze() - congeals a human review decision (MAP_TO_EXISTING/CREATE_NEW/REJECT on a taxonomy_candidate_concept_links row, or PUBLISH_RELATION/REJECT on a taxonomy_concept_relations row) into an immutable taxonomy_reviewed_proposals row with payload_fingerprint (tamper detection) and taxonomy_state_fingerprint (staleness detection, same CanonicalConceptBuilderService::dryRunInputFingerprint() as Phase C1). Never rediscovers or recomputes the proposal - never calls dryRun()/scoredCandidatesForTerm(). Never writes to taxonomy_term_concepts/taxonomy_canonical_concepts/taxonomy_concept_relations. Never touches the source candidate/relation's status.
contract_implemented.apply: ReviewedProposalService::apply(proposalId, authorizationReference) - authorizationReference required, non-empty, must contain a digit (same format convention as CanonicalConceptApplyService::apply()); target_environment auto-captured via app()->environment(), never caller-supplied. Inside one DB transaction: lockForUpdate() the payload row (idempotent replay if already APPLIED/ABORTED, no new writes), recompute and compare payload_fingerprint (tamper), recompute and compare taxonomy_state_fingerprint (staleness), lockForUpdate() and re-verify the real candidate/relation entity's current status (server-side, independent of the frozen payload), re-run validateConceptRelationProposal() with excludeId for PUBLISH_RELATION (same mechanism as TASK-0003 finding 6), only then write and mark the payload APPLIED - or write an explicit ABORTED status with a specific reason if any check fails. Every apply()/abort() outcome is audited via TaxonomyAuditLogger with authorization_reference/target_environment populated (actor_type=system) - distinct from freeze()'s review-time audit entry, which deliberately has neither field populated (actor_type=user).

finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.defect: TaxonomyReviewedProposalPolicy::view() used OR semantics over both permission families, so a user allowed to view candidate links could open a RELATION proposal's detail and vice versa. Worse, viewAny() plus an unscoped Resource table meant a user with permission for only ONE source type could list proposals of BOTH.
finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.fix: view() now resolves by proposal_type (TYPE_TERM_CONCEPT_LINK requires view_taxonomy::candidate::concept::link, TYPE_CONCEPT_RELATION requires view_taxonomy::concept::relation, an unknown type returns false as a closed default). viewAny() deliberately stays OR because it is the permission to ENTER the list and someone who can see at least one type must be able to open it - that boolean is not what closed the leak. The leak is closed by a new TaxonomyReviewedProposalResource::getEloquentQuery() override that filters rows to the types the user may list, via the new TaxonomyReviewedProposalPolicy::visibleProposalTypes() helper (returns [] with no permissions, and whereIn(..., []) compiles to 0 = 1, i.e. zero rows - no sentinel type needed). canAccess() was rewritten on that same helper so it cannot drift from the policy.
finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.direct_url_also_closed: ViewRecord resolves its record against getEloquentQuery(), so a proposal of a non-permitted type does not resolve (404) in addition to the 403 the per-type view() policy would return - two independent layers, and the tests accept either status as 'denied' while separately asserting the policy boolean directly.
finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.super_admin: No special-casing and no bypass. Inherited from the project's normal permission model (Shield grants every permission to the super_admin role), so both per-type checks return true through the ordinary path.
finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.tests: 9 tests: candidate-only viewer, relation-only viewer, both-permissions viewer and unauthorized viewer, covering BOTH list visibility and direct detail URL access, plus a per-persona scoped-query test and an exact row-identity test.
finding_1_authorization_leak_across_sour.assertion_level_note: The three list-visibility tests assert on the list page's QUERY rather than on rendered HTML (assertCanSeeTableRecords), for a real local-environment reason, and this is stronger evidence rather than weaker. Two facts combine: (a) AdminPanelProvider::boot() applies Table::configureUsing(fn ($t) => $t->deferLoading()) to EVERY table in the panel, so the initial mount renders only the shell and rows arrive in a second request via wire:init="loadTable" - without triggering that load any assertCanNotSeeTableRecords would pass trivially against an empty table; (b) triggering the load renders Filament's pagination view, which calls Number::format() and therefore requires ext-intl, absent in this local Windows environment (the same pre-existing limitation that blocks one TASK-0002 test, and present on the real staging runtime). So the tests assert on ListRecords::getTableQuery(), which returns VERBATIM static::getResource()::getEloquentQuery() and is the table's only source of rows - and each test also asserts that equivalence (SQL + bindings), so if anyone ever overrode getTableQuery() on the page the test fails instead of silently going stale. It asserts exact row identity per persona, not the presence of markup. This also retroactively explains the wire:init observed on staging in round 1: it was the panel's deferLoading(), not a problem.

finding_2_relation_resource_legacy_edit_.single_predicate: New TaxonomyConceptRelation::isUnderC2Review() - status===candidate OR a PENDING_APPLY reviewed proposal exists. section_D_architecture_finding.question: Is a single term architecturally allowed to have multiple approved canonical-concept mappings, and if so how is context/disambiguation represented and consumed?
section_D_architecture_finding.schema_permits_it: YES, physically. taxonomy_term_concepts (migration 2026_09_18_092000) declares UNIQUE (term_id, concept_id) - the constraint is on the PAIR, not on term_id alone - and TaxonomyTerm::concepts() is a belongsToMany.
section_D_architecture_finding.but_no_context_representation_exists: The pivot has exactly four columns: id, term_id, concept_id, created_at. There is NO context, condition, priority or disambiguation column - nowhere to express 'this concept applies in this context and that one in that other'. Context machinery does exist but only at TERM level (taxonomy_terms.context_required, positive_context, negative_context, context_window_words, minimum_supporting_terms, ambiguity_penalty), which cannot say WHICH of a term's N concepts applies in a given text.
section_D_architecture_finding.search_consumer_behaviour: BuildEmpresaSearchDocuments builds the index with three UNION branches; the third is concept-sibling expansion: a term with no approved direct CPV relations inherits the approved CPV categories of sibling terms sharing its concept (join taxonomy_term_concepts link on link.term_id = t.id, then sib_link on sib_link.concept_id = link.concept_id and sib_link.term_id != t.id, then approved taxonomy_term_cpv_relations). The join over `link` is NOT restricted to one concept and there is NO context gate in the query.
section_D_architecture_finding.conclusion: The architecture does NOT safely support multiple approved TERM->CONCEPT mappings. A polysemous term mapped to N concepts would unconditionally inherit the UNION of the CPV categories of every one of those concepts' sibling terms, with no context gate - precisely the outcome the comment forbids ('it must not automatically fan the term out to every superficially related CPV category').
section_D_architecture_finding.decision_taken: Following the branch the comment itself anticipated: TASK-0006A keeps the UI single-concept (MAP_TO_EXISTING with exactly one target_concept_id, plus CONTEXT_REQUIRED). No multi-select was added. Mapping cardinality was not touched.
section_D_architecture_finding.recorded_as_future_design_task: Multi-concept contextual mapping requires a NEW orchestrator gate because it would change search semantics and invalidate inherited search-regression evidence. Minimum it would need: a per-mapping context representation (new column/table on the pivot) AND a search consumer able to disambiguate - neither exists today.

reported_item_1_candidates_270_271.items: 270 `refinery` (en, technical_term) and 271 `refineria` (es, translation_alias with canonical_term='refinery', region LATAM)
reported_item_1_candidates_270_271.meaning_is_clear: A refinery is a concrete downstream processing facility and no canonical concept exists for it today (zero duplicates, zero explorer matches). The ambiguity is NOT semantic.
reported_item_1_candidates_270_271.what_is_actually_blocked: They are a BILINGUAL PAIR of the same concept and BOTH candidates propose the identical new concept name `refinery`. (1) Freezing CREATE_NEW on both would create two duplicate concepts - verified in apply()'s code, which creates the concept populating only ONE name field depending on the term's language, so for 271 (es) it would set canonical_name_es='refinery', i.e. the ENGLISH word in the Spanish field. (2) MAP_TO_EXISTING cannot be frozen on one pointing at the other's concept, because that concept would only exist after an APPLY, which is not authorised - freeze() validates the target concept exists.
reported_item_1_candidates_270_271.conclusion: The correct sequence (create the concept from one, then link the sibling) is NOT expressible with the available C2 decisions without an intermediate authorised APPLY, and the desired bilingual identity does not fit CREATE_NEW's single new_concept_name payload. Left pending with zero proposals rather than guessed.
reported_item_1_candidates_270_271.what_needs_deciding: The concept's canonical ES and EN names; the order of resolution given that linking the second term requires the concept to already exist (likely an authorised APPLY between the two decisions); or whether a new capability is warranted (CREATE_NEW accepting ES and EN names, and/or grouping several terms into one new concept) - which would be design work with its own gate, not part of TASK-0006.

reported_item_2_relations_61_62.items: Relation 61 `production / production` -> `production casing` (confidence 0.537, shared_cpv=1, name_similarity=0.6111, term_or_alias_overlap=0, weight=0) and relation 62 `oil / oil` -> `oil-base mud` (confidence 0.4359, shared_cpv=1, name_similarity=0.3077, term_or_alias_overlap=0). Both are automatic non-directional RELATED_TO proposals from CanonicalConceptBuilderService::proposeConceptRelations (canonical-concept-builder/phase-c-v1).
reported_item_2_relations_61_62.reading: Both rest on lexical similarity driven by a shared GENERIC word with zero term/alias overlap. For 61 the similarity comes entirely from the shared word 'production'; the relation is not false (production casing is used in production wells) but it is incidental. For 62 a real relationship exists but it is COMPOSITIONAL (the mud is oil-based), which RELATED_TO does not capture well, and the proposal arose from lexical similarity.
reported_item_2_relations_61_62.why_not_decided: Admitting or rejecting weak RELATED_TO edges derived from a shared generic word is a CURATION POLICY decision, and the project declares no confidence/evidence threshold for concept-to-concept relations. Deciding without that policy would be guessing the taxonomy owner's intent - exactly what the instruction forbids.
reported_item_2_relations_61_62.what_needs_deciding: An explicit criterion (e.g. a minimum confidence threshold, or a rule that term_or_alias_overlap=0 with similarity driven by a generic word is sufficient grounds to reject), or a case-by-case decision by the owner. Both relations remain status=candidate with zero proposals.
reported_item_2_relations_61_62.side_note: If 62 were to be published, the semantically correct relation type might not be RELATED_TO - but changing the proposed type is not a review decision, it is a different proposal.
